caption: Figure 1: The three stage compression pipeline: pruning, quantization and Huffman coding. Pruning reduces the number of weights by 10 × , while quantization further improves the compression rate: between 27 × and 31 × . Huffman coding gives more compression: between 35 × and 49 × . The compression rate already included the meta-data for sparse representation. The compression scheme doesn't incur any accuracy loss.
description:
This is a flow diagram showing a three-stage compression pipeline for deep neural networks. It includes pruning, quantization, and Huffman coding. Pruning reduces the number of weights by 9x-13x. Quantization further compresses the weights, achieving a 27x-31x reduction. Huffman coding provides additional compression, resulting in a 35x-49x reduction. The process maintains the same accuracy throughout.

Text in figure: Pruning: less number of weights, Quantization: less bits per weight, Huffman Encoding, Train Connectivity, original network, original size, Prune Connections, Train Weights, Cluster the Weights, Generate Code Book, same accuracy, Encode Weights, same accuracy, 9x-13x reduction, Quantize the Weights with Code Book, 27x-31x reduction, Encode Index, same accuracy, 35x-49x reduction, Retrain Code Book.

caption: Figure 6: Accuracy v.s. compression rate under different compression methods. Pruning and quantization works best when combined.
description:
Section 1: Figure description
This figure is a line graph comparing the accuracy loss of different compression methods for a deep neural network. The x-axis represents the model size ratio after compression, ranging from 2% to 20%. The y-axis represents the accuracy loss, ranging from -4.5% to 0.5%. Four series are plotted: Pruning + Quantization, Pruning Only, Quantization Only, and SVD. The Pruning + Quantization series has the lowest accuracy loss, followed by Quantization Only, Pruning Only, and SVD.

caption: Figure 7: Pruning doesn't hurt quantization. Dashed: quantization on unpruned network. Solid: quantization on pruned network; Accuracy begins to drop at the same number of quantization bits whether or not the network has been pruned. Although pruning made the number of parameters less, quantization still works well, or even better(3 bits case on the left figure) as in the unpruned network.
description:
Description: This figure contains three line graphs showing the accuracy of neural networks with varying numbers of bits per effective weight in fully connected (FC) layers, convolutional (Conv) layers, and all layers. Each graph has two series: one for networks quantized only and one for networks pruned and then quantized. The series for pruned and quantized networks is consistently higher, indicating better accuracy.

caption: Figure 11: Storage ratio of weight, index and codebook.
description:
This figure is a set of four pie charts, each representing the storage ratio of different components in various neural network architectures. The components are Weight, Index, and Codebook. The networks shown are AlexNet, VGGNet, Lenet-300-100, and Lenet-5. The Weight component is the largest in all charts, followed by Index, and Codebook is the smallest. AlexNet has the highest Weight percentage (51.4%) and the lowest Codebook percentage (0.1%). VGGNet has the highest Index percentage (51.8%) and the lowest Codebook percentage (0.1%). Lenet-300-100 has the highest Codebook percentage (1.5%). Lenet-5 has the highest Index percentage (53.8%) and the lowest Weight percentage (41.0%).
